name: Recruitment

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Recruitment

Player characters might decide to part with some of
their hard-earned gold and silver to take on a few
hirelings to help out during their next adventure,
but where do they look to find such august persons?
Luckily, nearly every town and settlement plays host
to no shortage of individuals looking for work. And
one never has to go far to find suitable help, for these
potential hirelings flock to places where they might
find employment. A quick trip to the docks can elicit
a dozen or more offers to resolve all manner of needs,
from those of hauling and lifting, to those of a more
intimate nature. Similarly, hotels, high-class inns,
coaching stations, and other venues of a like kind
attract the hungry and eager.
The abundance of offers says little about the
quality of the individuals in search of pay. After all,
if they were competent, might they not already have
gainful employment? A discerning employer never
accepts the first offer and takes the time to conduct
a proper interview in order to ascertain the merits
and flaws of the hireling. Doing so weeds out those
with insurmountable defects and ensures one finds
qualified candidates able and willing to perform all
the functions of the job described.
This said, the number of prospective candidates
depends largely on the nature of the work and the
size of the community. Any yokel can be convinced to
hold a lantern for a few coins, but scholars of ancient
esoteric lore don’t often quarter in rude hamlets
on the thinly populated fringe of civilization’s vast
tapestry. Similarly, a seemingly qualified contender
for a difficult and dangerous job in some far-flung
village ought to raise alarms; such people don’t often
wind up in such places without good reason. It pays to
inquire into the interviewee’s history and references to
dodge avoidable shenanigans.

2

name: Skill and Availability

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Skill and Availability
Each hireling has a skill rating, which determines
their availability and capabilities. The skill rating is
a number from 0 to 5, with 0 being unskilled and 5
being quite proficient. Skill rating 0 characters tend
to be laborers with little to no formal training. A
trained fighter might be skill rating 3 and a magicuser would be 5. The first table that follows shows
sample professions by skill rating, while the second
table shows availability and price using the scale
introduced in Shadow.

name: Background

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Background

1–2

Fled from war, plague, or something else and
works as a hireling to get back on their feet.

3–4

After failing in another trade, the hireling took
whatever job was available.

5–6

Becoming a hireling gives the character a way
out from a terrible situation, place to live, or bad
relationship.

7–8

Becoming a hireling is part of a new identity the
character has adopted to escape justice, enemies,
or a vengeful cult.

9–10

The hireling went on a few adventures and has a
hankering to get back into the business.

11–12

The hireling bears a curse that compels service to
other would-be heroes.

13–14

The hireling is looking for something and sees an
opportunity to find it by accompanying the group.

15–16

The hireling has nothing better to do.

17–18

The hireling craves recognition and believes that
working in this way will provide it.

19–20

The hireling has severe amnesia.

name: Loyalty Score

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Loyalty Score
Every hireling has a loyalty score, which fluctuates
depending on what happens during the adventure.
The GM determines the starting score by rolling a
d3 + half the group level for each hireling, keeping
the loyalty scores secret. The score changes often and
for a variety of reasons, as explained below.

name: Loyalty Loss

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Loyalty Loss
Bad circumstances cause hirelings to lose loyalty. Each
time a bad circumstance occurs, deduct the indicated
number from the hireling’s loyalty.

For each hireling, the GM makes a Will challenge
roll. The GM makes the roll with 1 boon if the
hireling’s loyalty is 3 or higher and 1 bane if it is 0. If
a hireling has negative loyalty, it gets an automatic
failure. On a success, the hireling’s loyalty holds for
6 rounds and is not subject to loyalty tests during this
time. On a failure, the hireling’s loyalty drops by 1d3.
If the hireling reaches 0 or lower loyalty, roll on the
Failed Loyalty table to see what happens.

Bad Circumstances

name: Testing Loyalty

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Testing Loyalty
Even the most constant servants think twice about
throwing their lives away, so hirelings, who normally
have little reason to go above and beyond what their
contract stipulates, most likely flee danger, especially
when said danger could mean their very lives. In

6

situations where the outcome looks dire, the GM
might test the hirelings’ loyalty. Such situations
include, but are not limited to, all of the following.
• A player character becomes incapacitated.
• Another hireling dies.
• Enemy combatants number more than twice the
group’s numbers.
• A player character becomes subject to madness.
• The hireling gains Insanity or becomes frightened.

Good Circumstances
